rooms.prompt:

pair keeps n in s0, and sq(n) in s1 while it makes the second call.

rooms.hint: List every register pair writes that its caller expects back unchanged, and the one its calls overwrite.
rooms.explanation: A function that keeps two values across its calls uses two s registers, so it saves both, and it saves ra because it makes calls. Leaving out any one of the three breaks the contract in its own way.

rooms.prompt:

diff keeps x in s0, and cube(x) in s1 while it makes the second call.

rooms.hint: Which kind of register does a function have to give back unchanged: t or s?
rooms.explanation: A function saves the s registers it uses (and ra, if it calls), because its caller expects them back. t registers are scratch: cube may use t0, and saving t0 in diff's frame protects nothing anyone expects back.

rooms.prompt:
Build sum's frame and outrun the Chomper.
The Chomper climbs up from the heap while sum(5) adds 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1.
rooms.code_snippet: int sum(int n) { return n <= 0 ? 0 : n + sum(n - 1); }
rooms.hint: sum needs ra and the s0 it keeps n in. Anything more makes every floor bigger.
rooms.explanation: Two words, ra and s0, is the tightest frame that works, so the stack stays ahead of the Chomper. A bigger frame still works here, but every extra word is paid on every floor.

code.ask: The Chomper eats a stack word every 4 instructions, and sum(5) needs six floors. sum's frame saves:

options.label: ra, s0, and t0
options.why: Three words a floor: sum(5) still finishes first, but by a single word.

options.label: only ra
options.why: n lived in s0, and nothing saved it: every floor added the bottom floor's n (1), so sum returned 5 instead of 15, and the Chomper's s0 came back changed.

options.label: ra and s0
options.why: Two words a floor: sum(5) has room to spare.

code.note: n <= 0 is the bottom floor: it returns 0.
Keep n.
One floor down: sum(n - 1).
Back up: n + sum(n - 1).
